problems.question: A spaceship has a weight of 10000 N on Mars, where \(g_{\text{Mars}} = 3.7\,\text{ms}^{-2}\). What would be the spaceship's weight on Earth? (\(g_{\text{Earth}} = 9.8\,\text{ms}^{-2}\))
problems.hint: Find the mass using Mars' gravity, then calculate the weight on Earth.
problems.author: Sofia Osorio

problems.question: An astronaut has a mass of 80 kg. What is the astronaut’s weight on the Moon? (\(g_{\text{Moon}} = 1.6\,\text{ms}^{-2}\))
problems.hint: Weight depends on the gravitational field strength.
problems.author: Filip Kilibarda

problems.question: A box has a mass of 5 kg. What is its weight on Earth? (\(g = 9.8\,\text{ms}^{-2}\))
problems.author: Filip Kilibarda

problems.question: A person weighs 686 N on Earth. What is the person’s mass? (\(g = 9.8\,\text{ms}^{-2}\))
problems.author: Filip Kilibarda

problems.question: A satellite has a mass of 1200 kg. Which statement about its mass and weight is correct as it moves from Earth into deep space?
options: Mass decreases but weight stays constant
Mass stays constant but weight decreases
Both mass and weight stay constant
problems.hint: Mass is intrinsic; weight depends on gravity.
problems.detailed: Mass does not depend on location, so it remains constant. Weight depends on gravitational field strength, which decreases in deep space.
problems.author: Filip Kilibarda
